text: 🍿 Mr. Irrelevant: the last pick who made it count 📆 Estreno: December 25, 2026 🎭 Género: #Drama #Sports #Biopic ✈️ Add to watchlist David Corenswet carries this thing on pure screen presence. Classic jaw, Golden Age magnetism, the kind of face Paramount used to build careers around. Good fit for a story that needs you to believe in a guy nobody believed in. John Tuggle was the very last pick of the 1983 NFL Draft. Dead at 25 from cancer. That is not a feel-good arc; it is a gut punch with a jersey on. Michael Shannon in the supporting cast suggests Paramount isn't playing it safe. The real question is whether the film earns the tragedy or soft-pedals it into sports-movie wallpaper. The trailer hints at both. Cautiously on board.

🍿 The Odyssey just became Universal's biggest film ever. And WB handed it to them. Christopher Nolan's gamble on theaters paid off to the tune of $1.68 billion worldwide, dethroning Jurassic World as Universal's all-time record holder. Matt Damon as Odysseus, a 97% audience score, and the best reviews of Nolan's career. WB let him walk over a streaming policy. During COVID, they couldn't commit to theatrical exclusivity, and Nolan walked. He then made Oppenheimer and now this. That's two of the biggest films of the decade, gone. For a policy they've since abandoned. This is what happens when a studio misjudges its own asset. Nolan is one of the few directors whose name alone sells tickets. You don't fumble that. ✈️ Add to watchlist

🎬 Taron Egerton is the most wanted man in London. Not by the police. Director Jonathan Schey inverts the predatory-dating dynamic entirely: the women stalk, Egerton's "nice guy" Adam is the target. Sharp satirical premise, backed by Film4, StudioCanal, and LuckyChap, and clearly self-aware about every inch of its title. The title stays. Good. Egerton playing a murky, likeable-but-not charmer is smarter casting than it first appears, and this kind of dark British comedy with actual teeth is exactly what Film4 does best. ✈️ Add to watchlist
